title: UTF-8 Validation
description: Given an integer array `data` where only the least significant 8 bits of each element represent a byte, return `true` if `data` forms a valid sequence of UTF-8 characters under the byte-prefix rules, and `false` otherwise. Valid characters use 1 to 4 bytes: 1-byte `0xxxxxxx`; 2-byte `110xxxxx 10xxxxxx`; 3-byte `1110xxxx 10xxxxxx 10xxxxxx`; 4-byte `11110xxx 10xxxxxx 10xxxxxx 10xxxxxx`.
hints: Maintain a counter `remaining` of how many continuation bytes (`10xxxxxx`) are still expected for the current character.
When `remaining == 0`, inspect the leading bits of `byte & 0xFF` to determine whether the character has 0, 1, 2, or 3 continuation bytes; reject any byte starting with `10` or five or more `1`s.

examples.explanation: 197 (11000101) starts a 2-byte char followed by continuation 130 (10000010), then 1 (00000001) is a 1-byte char.
235 (11101011) expects two continuation bytes, but 4 (00000100) does not start with 10.
240 (11110000) is a 4-byte header followed by three valid 10xxxxxx continuation bytes.
